messages:
Jordan: Customer reported spikes of 5-10s tail latency and intermittent 502s from Dedicated cluster A (eu-west-1). Key req IDs: r-0a1f2b3c, r-0d4e5f6a, r-0b7c8d9e. Seen between 2026-03-16T14:05:00Z and 14:12:00Z. Can SRE capture pod + node logs and a GPU metrics snapshot?
Alex: Seen similar before when a node had GPU driver OOMs. I'll start with a quick check. Which namespace + deployment?
Jordan: Namespace: redwood-dedicated-prod, deployment: runtime-v2. Pods: runtime-v2-0, runtime-v2-1, runtime-v2-2. Affected customer reported requests routed to runtime-v2-1.
Maya: Can we get a curl repro from the customer? Ask them to include X-Request-ID header and the exact body. If we can reproduce we can pin down where latency appears (proxy vs runtime). Example curl we can give:
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1f2b3c" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello world","max_tokens":50}' \
  https://dedicated-eu-west-1.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Jordan: Sent that to the customer, they replied with a curl including the same X-Request-ID and the same latency. They gave a sample response headers showing upstream: 502 and request_time: 7.12s.
Ricardo: I'll pull pod logs for runtime-v2-1 for the window. Running: `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated-prod logs runtime-v2-1 --since=20m --tail=200`. Also check sidecar/proxy: `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated-prod logs runtime-v2-1 -c envoy --since=20m`.
Ricardo: Also running `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated-prod describe pod runtime-v2-1` to check events (OOMKills, restarts).
Alex: I grabbed the envoy logs; there's a repeating message around 14:08:22: `upstream request timeout while reading response header from upstream` followed by 502. Runtime logs show long GC pause entries and frequent garbage-collector wakes. Snippet: `2026-03-16T14:08:21Z runtime INFO [kv-cache] GC pause 3250ms; heap=1.8G`.
Sheila: Can you collect node-level logs and GPU metrics where runtime-v2-1 was scheduled? Node is gke-eu-west-1-node-7. Commands to run: `journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-16 14:00:00"` and `kubectl -n kube-system logs node-exporter-gke-eu-west-1-node-7`. For GPU: run `kubectl debug node/gke-eu-west-1-node-7 -it --image=nvidia/cuda:11.7-base -- bash` then `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-sample.csv --count=5`.
Jordan: Customer also provided a small trace token: tracer:abc123 (span shows long wait in runtime pre-proc). Might be KV cache heavy.
Maya: Can we get a debug bundle from the node and pod for the timeframe? Use our debug-collector: `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated-prod exec runtime-v2-1 -c runtime -- ./collector.sh --since "2026-03-16T14:00:00Z" --until "2026-03-16T14:15:00Z" --out /tmp/debug-runtime-v2-1.tar.gz` then `kubectl cp`. For node: `sudo /opt/redwood/debug/collect_node_bundle.sh --since "2026-03-16 14:00:00" --out /tmp/node-bundle.tar.gz` via debug container.
Ricardo: I pulled the pod logs + envoy and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support-dumps/1763123456/runtime-v2-1-logs.tar.gz. The runtime logs include repeated `malloc failed` warnings around 14:07:58 — looks like mem pressure. Pod events show kubelet evicting cache.
Alex: I also ran `nvidia-smi` on node snapshot and got this (sample):
```
Timestamp, Name, Utilization.gpu [%], Utilization.memory [%], Memory.total [MiB], Memory.used [MiB]
2026-03-16T14:06:30, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, 12 %, 6 %, 81920 MiB, 5200 MiB
2026-03-16T14:07:30, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, 98 %, 94 %, 81920 MiB, 77000 MiB
2026-03-16T14:08:30, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, 99 %, 96 %, 81920 MiB, 78800 MiB
```
Alex: GPU memory shot up just before the timeout window — likely a bad batch or ineffective kv-cache eviction + large prompt causing OOM-ish behavior in userspace (alloc failing, GC spike).
Sheila: For next steps: 1) keep runtime-v2-1 cordoned while we repro. `kubectl cordon gke-eu-west-1-node-7` 2) get full debug bundles from node + pod and attach to ticket 54321 3) if repro confirmed, add a guard to reject requests with input size > X or fallback to a smaller model.
Jordan: Customer gave permission to collect debug bundle and is available for a 15min window at 14:40Z to reproduce. I'll schedule a short repro with them and include the X-Request-ID header.
Ricardo: After cordon, I re-deployed runtime-v2 with a burn-in to repro. Repro curl with the customer's payload produced a 6.9s delay then success on runtime-v2-2 (different node). The trace shows the delay inside model runtime during kv retrieval: several large cache misses.
Maya: Sounds like KV cache eviction policy might be thrashing under certain access patterns. I'll open an internal ticket to run a targeted workload test and a hotfix to bump cache size and add diagnostic metrics per-request (kv hits/misses).
Alex: Logging next: add per-request memory accounting and sample stack traces on alloc failures. For immediate mitigation, Sheila, can you add an autoscaling rule to limit max concurrent requests per GPU instance?
Sheila: Will do. Added temporary rate-limit in the autoscaler config and removed burst capacity on that pool. Rolling change applied at 14:23Z.
Jordan: Thanks all — I'll post the repro window and S3 links in the support ticket and confirm with the customer after the 14:40Z run. :thumbsup: 
sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-03016-01, severity: low-medium, assigned: eng-runtime, linked_ticket: 54321.
